summary: Union County Forestry Commission tower; sold at auction in 2010 for $4,024. No source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Sold at auction in 2010. No source says whether the tower still stands.

events.note: Sold at auction for $4024.00 (Forest Lookouts record).

evidence.supports: Kelly is a South Carolina Forestry Commission tower

evidence.quote: 2010: The tower was sold at auction for $4024.00.

evidence.supports: The network began with a tower near Camden in August 1930
evidence.quote: The first Forestry Commission fire tower was erected in August, 1930 near Camden.

evidence.supports: Towers ranged from about 55 to 120 feet tall
evidence.quote: South Carolina towers ranged from about 55′ tall (atop Sassafras Mountain in Pickens County) to 120′ tall.

evidence.supports: The agency closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

evidence.supports: The Kelly Tower in Union County was among towers the agency was selling to the highest bidder
evidence.quote: the Kelly Tower in Union County

evidence.supports: Blog: it seems the agency is selling several towers to the highest bidder
evidence.quote: It seems that the South Carolina Forestry Commission is selling several of its lookout towers to the highest bidder.
Bidding for the towers starts at $500.

evidence.supports: Most towers in the sale had no bids yet
evidence.quote: Most of these currently have no bids

evidence.supports: The purchaser was responsible for removing the tower
evidence.quote: The purchaser is responsible for removing the tower.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The sources here give the 2010 auction price, the agency listing and the blog's description of the sale, but no build date, height or staffing for Kelly. The blog post is undated, so it is not tied to the 2010 sale by year. Brief coordinates (34.8128, -81.6226) were not checked against a second source.
